# Rivers

```{r}
rivers<-st_read(here("projected_data/Rivers/Fiji_rivers.shp"))
```


# Basins

```{r}
# Read in data and calculate area
basins12<-st_read(here("raw_data/Basins/BasinATLAS_v10_lev12.shp"))

basins12_proj<-st_transform(basins12, st_crs(rivers))

#st_write(basins12_proj, here("projected_data/Basins/AllBasins12.shp"))

#basins12_proj<-st_read(here("projected_data/Basins/AllBasins12.shp"))

rivers_proj<-st_transform(rivers, st_crs(basins12))
```

# Pourpoints
Method from here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55106950/r-sf-intersect-lines-with-the-borders-of-multipolygons-extract-coordinates-of

Here is the new method I should use: https://gis.stackexchange.com/questions/251101/return-end-vertices-of-an-sf-linestring

```{r}
# Read in data
sub_fiji_rivers<- rivers_proj %>% 
  filter(NEXT_DOWN == 0) %>% 
  st_cast(., "LINESTRING")


#If you only want the endpoints, then st_line_sample is what you are looking for:

pnts<-st_endpoint(sub_fiji_rivers) 

pnts_xy<-st_coordinates(pnts) 

data_per_river<-st_join(sub_fiji_rivers,basins12)
data_per_river<-data_per_river[!duplicated(data_per_river$HYRIV_ID),]

data_per_river<-st_transform(data_per_river, st_crs(rivers)) %>% 
  rename(riv_dis = dis_m3_pyr.x,
         bas_dis = dis_m3_pyr.y)

pnts<-st_transform(pnts, st_crs(rivers))

pb <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = nrow(data_per_river), style = 3) 
pour_points<-list()
for (i in 1:nrow(data_per_river)){
  setTxtProgressBar(pb, i)
  points_line<- st_cast(data_per_river[i,], "POINT")
  pour_points[[i]]<- points_line[nrow(points_line),]
  data_per_river[i,"pp_x"]<-extent(pour_points[[i]])[1]
  data_per_river[i,"pp_y"]<-extent(pour_points[[i]])[3]
  
}

```



# Nutrients per basin

```{r}
septic_basins_nutri<-read.csv(here("output_data/Nutrients/N_P_septic_per_basin.csv")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-X)

direct_basins_nutri<-read.csv(here("output_data/Nutrients/N_P_direct_per_basin.csv")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-X)
```


# Distribute

We distributed the sediment export across all points weighted by the mean annual discharge of each river

```{r}
septic_basins_nutri_all<-left_join(data_per_river, septic_basins_nutri, by = c("MAIN_BAS")) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  dplyr::select(-geometry, MAIN_BAS, riv_dis)

direct_basins_nutri_all<-left_join(data_per_river, direct_basins_nutri, by = c("MAIN_BAS")) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  dplyr::select(-geometry, MAIN_BAS, riv_dis)

septic_basins_nutri_dist<-septic_basins_nutri_all %>% 
  group_by(MAIN_BAS) %>% 
  summarise(Total_discharge = sum(riv_dis)) %>% 
  left_join(., septic_basins_nutri_all, by = "MAIN_BAS") %>% 
  mutate(prop_dis = riv_dis/Total_discharge,
         N_pourpoint = prop_dis * N,
         P_pourpoint = prop_dis * P)

direct_basins_nutri_dist<-direct_basins_nutri_all %>% 
  group_by(MAIN_BAS) %>% 
  summarise(Total_discharge = sum(riv_dis)) %>% 
  left_join(., direct_basins_nutri_all, by = "MAIN_BAS") %>% 
  mutate(prop_dis = riv_dis/Total_discharge,
         N_pourpoint = prop_dis * N,
         P_pourpoint = prop_dis * P)

write_csv(septic_basins_nutri_dist, here("output_data/Nutrients/Fiji_septic_nutrients_at_pourpoints.csv"))

write_csv(direct_basins_nutri_dist, here("output_data/Nutrients/Fiji_direct_nutrients_at_pourpoints.csv"))
  
```

# Nutrient export at each pourpoint

```{r}
pour_points<-septic_basins_nutri_dist
coordinates(pour_points) <- ~pp_x+pp_y
pour_points<-st_as_sf(pour_points)
pour_points<-pour_points %>% 
  dplyr::select(HYRIV_ID, MAIN_BAS, N_pourpoint, P_pourpoint) %>% 
  rename(N = N_pourpoint,
         P = P_pourpoint) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(N) == T)

st_crs(pour_points)<-"+proj=tmerc +lat_0=-17 +lon_0=178.75 +k=0.9998548 +x_0=2000000 +y_0=4000000 +ellps=WGS72 +units=m +no_defs "

st_write(pour_points, here("output_data/Rivers/Fiji_septic_pourpoints.shp"), delete_layer = T)
```

# Diffusion model

Avoid reprojecting ocean if possible - takes awhile

```{r}
#ocean_raster<-raster(here("raw_data/Global/oceans_moll.tif"))

#ocean_raster<-projectRaster(ocean_raster, crs = as.character(crs(stp_pp_proj)))

#writeRaster(ocean_raster, here("projected_data/oceans_moll_proj.tif"))

ocean_raster<-raster(here("projected_data/oceans_moll_proj.tif"))
```


```{r}
gc()
p_extent=st_as_sfc(st_bbox(pour_points))
p_extent_sub = st_make_grid(p_extent,n = c(40,20)) %>%
               st_as_sf() %>% 
               rename(geom=x) %>%
               mutate(group=1:nrow(.))
tmap::tm_shape(p_extent_sub)+tmap::tm_polygons()
pour_points = st_join(pour_points, p_extent_sub, join = st_intersects) %>% 
              mutate(ID=1:nrow(.)) %>% 
  as_Spatial

  point_list<-split(pour_points,as.character(pour_points@data$ID))
  re = pbmcapply::pbmclapply(point_list, N_plume, ocean_raster, 80000, c(1110,894), 90000, mc.cores = 10)
  #Check to see if we should change buffer value
  
  # Set extent for all outputs to the max extent needed, e.g., newextent
  newextent<-extent(Reduce(extend,re)) # Get max extent of all objects
  re_ext=mclapply(re, extend, newextent, mc.cores=1) # Use fewer cores as this gets more memory heavy
  gc()
  
  # Reclass NAs to 0
  re_ext = mclapply(re_ext, mc.cores = 1, function(x) reclassify(x, cbind(NA,0))) # Reclass NA to 0, in a more memory friendly way,apparently...
  gc()

  # Add all rasters in the group together + mask out land areas is desired
  sed_plume_merge = Reduce("+", re_ext) 
  sed_plume_merge = sed_plume_merge * ocean_raster # mask out land; disregard the warning
  
  writeRaster(sed_plume_merge, here(paste0("output_data/Nutrients/Fiji_septic_N_plumes.tif")))

```
